data.content_ref: inline:The stated 'refuted if' test is self-defeating: it attacks the relation only if the constant-difference shortcut yields 'a residue class not already capturable by the standard CRT parametric method' and is therefore 'a genuinely independent solution path.' But independence from the standard method is precisely what would make the abstraction relation substantive; a specialization that collapses into the standard parametric form is a dependence/reduction, not a refutation of the abstraction claim. Thus the refutation condition is backwards — it refutes the relation when the shortcut is shown to be distinct, and would pass it when it is redundant — so it does not supply a coherent test of the proposed abstraction/inheritance relation.
